input.quote: 5.3 Sublicenses. AbbVie shall have the right to grant sublicenses (or further rights of reference), through multiple tiers of Sublicensees, under the licenses and rights of reference granted in Sections 5.1.1, 5.1.2 and 5.1.3, to its Affiliates and other Persons
input.rationale: The grants to us in Sections 5.1.1–5.1.3 satisfy the LICENSE checklist at or above the fallback, so no redline is warranted. (i) Affiliates: Section 5.3 lets us sublicense through multiple tiers to our Affiliates and other Persons (which reaches contractors acting on our behalf) with no Harpoon consent, subject only to delivering a copy of the sublicense — better than the fallback's "covered on written notice"; Sections 5.4 and 5.5 confirm Affiliate distribution and co-promotion rights in our sole discretion. (ii) Successor transfer: Section 13.4.1 permits assignment without Harpoon's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, sale of stock or sale of assets. The licence is also not revocable at Harpoon's discretion — Harpoon may terminate only for uncured material breach (Section 12.2.1, 90-day cure) or insolvency (Section 12.4), while we hold the unilateral termination right in Section 12.3 — and on expiry of the Term the Section 5.1.3 grants become fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable (Section 12.1.2). Minor points short of the preferred wording, noted only: affiliate/contractor coverage runs through the sublicensing mechanic rather than the grant language itself, and Harpoon retains an insolvency termination right in addition to uncured material breach. Neither is material enough to reopen.
